title: Navigation API traversal: reject the finished promise when the traversable's navigate event is canceled (`canceled-by-navigate`)

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

[perform a navigation API traversal](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#performing-a-navigation-api-traversal) step 12.5 only handles `canceled-by-beforeunload`, and step 12.6 handles `initiator-disallowed`. [Check if unloading is canceled](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#checking-if-unloading-is-canceled) can also return `canceled-by-navigate`. That happens when the traversable's [traverse `navigate` event](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#fire-a-traverse-navigate-event) is canceled (step 4.3.4.5). Nothing in the algorithm handles that result.

The note after step 12.6 says the inner `navigate` event firing algorithm takes care of this case. It does so by aborting the ongoing navigation in [step 28.2](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#inner-navigate-event-firing-algorithm). That only reaches the `Navigation` object the event fired at, which is the traversable's. It does not reach the `Navigation` of the subframe that called `traverseTo()`, `back()` or `forward()`.

**Repro:**

1. A top-level page has an iframe, and both have a same-document entry.
2. The top-level page sets `navigation.onnavigate = e => e.preventDefault()`.
3. The iframe calls `iframe.navigation.traverseTo(key)`.
4. The traversable's `navigate` event is canceled, so `finalStatus` is `canceled-by-navigate`.
5. Step 12.5 does not match, so the iframe's `committed` and `finished` promises stay pending.
6. The iframe's `apiMethodTracker` also stays in its [upcoming traverse API method trackers](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#upcoming-traverse-api-method-trackers). A later `traverseTo()` with the same key then returns the stale tracker's result at step 6, and never queues a new traversal.

**Proposal:** In step 12.5, also match `canceled-by-navigate`:

> If *result* is "`canceled-by-beforeunload`" or "`canceled-by-navigate`", then queue a global task ... to reject the finished promise for *apiMethodTracker* with a new "`AbortError`" `DOMException` ...

The note should then say that the traversable's own tracker is aborted by the inner algorithm, and that the initiating subframe's tracker is rejected here.

An intercepted traverse `navigate` event (`finalStatus` is `continue`) is unaffected. The traversal resumes, and the promises settle when it commits.

WPT already expects the rejection: [`navigation-api/navigate-event/navigation-traverseTo-in-iframe-same-document-preventDefault.html`](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/navigation-api/navigate-event/navigation-traverseTo-in-iframe-same-document-preventDefault.html) has the parent call `preventDefault()` on the traverse `navigate` event, then asserts the iframe's `committed` and `finished` reject with `AbortError` ("When the top window blocks the traversal, it should be blocked in the iframe as well, and the traversal promises in the iframe should be rejected."). The spec as written leaves those promises pending, so it needs to follow the test.

cc @farre @theIDinside @noamr
